name: Navrangpura
tagline: University-adjacent core with cafes and coworking
description: The old west-side hub around CG Road and Law Garden, packed with commercial towers, bookshops, chai stalls and the campuses of Gujarat University and CEPT. Students and office workers fill the pavements. It has the densest cluster of coworking desks and cafes you can reach on foot.
bestFor: Nomads who want coworking, cafes and a metro stop all within a short walk
pros: Most walkable commercial area in the city
Many coworking spaces and laptop-friendly cafes
Metro and buses connect the whole west side
cons: CG Road traffic and horn noise are relentless
Older buildings with unreliable lifts and parking
Very little green space or quiet

name: Vastrapur
tagline: Lake, malls and IIM, the balanced west-side pick
description: Built around Vastrapur Lake with its walking path and open-air amphitheatre, this district mixes mid-rise apartment societies, the Alpha One mall and the IIM Ahmedabad campus. It attracts students, faculty and young professionals. Rents sit below Bodakdev while keeping cafes, gyms and the metro close.
bestFor: Nomads who want a lakeside jog, a serviced flat and good value on the west side
pros: Lake and parks for morning walks
Strong mix of cafes, malls and grocery delivery
Metro station and easy autos everywhere
cons: Weekend crowds around the lake and malls
Society flats often demand long leases

name: Prahlad Nagar
tagline: Glass towers, garden and the modern expat pocket
description: A planned grid of new high-rises and corporate parks around the landscaped Prahlad Nagar Garden, just off SG Highway. Wide roads, gated societies with gyms and pools, plus a strip of upmarket restaurants and bakeries. It is where relocating professionals and long-stay foreigners generally land.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a new serviced apartment with a gym, pool and fast fibre
pros: Newest apartment stock with pools, gyms and backup power
Big landscaped garden and a jogging loop
Dense choice of restaurants and coworking on SG Highway
cons: Long walks between blocks in brutal summer heat
SG Highway traffic is heavy at peak hours

name: Bodakdev
tagline: Quiet bungalow lanes behind the business strip
description: A leafy pocket of bungalows, low-rise societies and the Thaltej Iskcon corridor, sitting immediately behind the SG Highway office towers. It is calmer than Prahlad Nagar but just as well served, with speciality coffee, delis and clinics. Popular with settled families and senior professionals.
bestFor: Nomads staying months who want a peaceful street but corporate infrastructure nearby
pros: Speciality cafes, gyms and good hospitals close by
Short hop to the SG Highway coworking cluster
cons: Expensive and mostly geared to families, not short stays
Sparse public transport inside the lanes

name: Old City
tagline: Walled heritage lanes, pols and the cheapest rents
description: The walled east bank around Manek Chowk, Bhadra Fort and the carved wooden pols, where the market flips from vegetables by day to a street food riot at night. It is the cheapest place to stay and the most atmospheric, but infrastructure is old and lanes are tight.
bestFor: Budget travellers and photographers who want heritage streets over comfort
pros: Cheapest rooms and food in the city
UNESCO listed heritage lanes and the best street food
Very central for the riverfront and heritage walks
cons: Congested, noisy lanes with poor air quality
Ageing buildings, patchy water and internet
Almost no coworking or laptop-friendly cafes
